facts.business: Andhra Paper Limited manufactures paper, paperboard, and pulp, and is entering the tissue and hygiene segment.

capacity_or_capex.item: Modernisation of manufacturing facilities across both operating units (Rajahmundry and Kadiam)
Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) additions during FY26

guidance_or_targets.statement: Wood inventory will be increased from 30 days to 50 days when wood availability is good.
Maturing plantation cycles will ease wood costs in FY2026-27, benefiting the Company's input cost structure.
EPR target for plastic waste collection for FY 2025-26 is 1268 tons.

auditor.name: Not explicitly stated in excerpts
auditor.emphasis_or_qualification: The Report of Auditors for the financial Year 2025-26 does not have any qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks. Unmodified opinion on IFC was given by them.

key_risks: Raw material risk: Structural wood fibre deficit, supply gaps impacting margins
Threat from cheaper imports: Rising cheaper imports from ASEAN countries and China at zero or reduced duty under FTA constraining domestic pricing power and realisations
Demand shifts: Structural changes from digitalisation and evolving consumption patterns moderating demand growth in writing and printing segments
Regulatory risk: Delayed compliance with Regulation 17(1A) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 resulting in fines
Input cost volatility: Volatile input costs including wood, pulp, and chemical prices
